title: Making ten to add 8 + 5
examples: What is the make ten strategy?
How do I add 8 and 5 in my head?
What does bridging through ten mean?

explain.say: 8 plus 5 looks tricky, but here is a secret: tens are easy. Look at the ten frame. There are 8 counters, and 5 more are coming. Watch where they go, and you will see the answer is 13.
First, fill the frame. 8 needs just 2 more to make 10. See the 2 new counters fill the last empty boxes? Now you have a full ten. How many of the 5 have you used?
You used 2, so 3 are left. They start a new frame. Now you can see a full 10 and 3 more, which makes 13. Can you see the two frames?
So 8 plus 5 equals 13. You split the 5 into 2 and 3, so one part makes ten. This is called making ten, or bridging ten. Bridging means going over, like a bridge. Can you try 9 plus 4 the same way?
Great thinking! 9 needs 1 to make 10, and 3 are left, so 9 plus 4 is 13. Children in Singapore and China learn this trick early, and it works for 29 plus 4 too. Can you do 7 plus 6?

faq.q: What is the make ten strategy?
faq.a: It is a way to add by filling up a ten first. For 8 plus 5, give 2 of the 5 to the 8 to make 10, then add the 3 left: 13.

faq.q: What does bridging through ten mean?
faq.a: Bridging means crossing over, like a bridge. You go up to 10 first, then over it with what is left. 8 plus 5 goes 8, then 10, then 13.
Because 8 needs exactly 2 to make 10. Your number bonds tell you that, and 5 is 2 and 3, so 3 are left over.
asks: How do I know how to split the number?

faq.q: Does making ten work with bigger numbers?
faq.a: Yes. For 28 plus 5, 28 needs 2 to make 30, then add the other 3 to get 33. It is the same trick.
asks: Can I use it for 28 plus 5?

faq.q: How do I add 7 and 6 by making ten?
faq.a: 7 needs 3 to make 10. Split 6 into 3 and 3. Then 10 plus 3 is 13, so 7 plus 6 equals 13.

facts: Making ten is a key mental strategy in the Singapore maths curriculum.

quiz.say: To add 9 plus 6 by making ten, how do you split the 6?
quiz.show: To add 9 + 6 by making ten, how do you split the 6?
quiz.why: 9 needs 1 to make 10, so split 6 into 1 and 5. Then 10 plus 5 is 15.

wrong.1: 3 and 3 gives 9 plus 3, which is 12, not a ten.
wrong.2: 9 plus 2 is 11, which goes past ten.

quiz.why: 7 needs 3 to make 10, and 2 are left, so 10 plus 2 is 12.

wrong.0: 11 is one short; a counter went missing.
